title: review: S4: skill scorecard with marginal value and redundancy: skill × role × task class × complexity × model × workflow strategy, role-without-skill vs role-with-skill comparison, redundancy between co-used skills; reporting only (v3)
spec:
Program brief .orchestrator/roadmap-skills.md P14, P15, P16, P24, P25, P30 (P37 stage 4). Depends on T-0894 (run context carries skills_exposed / skills_used / skill tokens; skill_scorecard.py exists with use_rate and overhead) and T-0913 (skills_selected, skill_recovery_rate). Facts: run rows (bus.log_run) carry role, task, tier/executor (model via attribution.model_of), usage tokens, usd, duration_s; lineage roots via attribution.lineage; task_class via attribution.task_class; complexity band via attribution.band; workflow strategy via strategy.derive(task, tasks); gate/review outcomes live on task pipelines (gate_reds, review verdicts on review tasks with inputs[0]); read_economy gate rows carry per-call paths and tools; promotion CRITERIA min_samples 20.
Do:
1. skill_scorecard.py: `usage_rows(root)` = one row per run with skills_used, plus the lineage's outcome (first_pass, fix_rounds, gate_reds, review_request_changes, accepted, accepted_tokens, accepted_usd, latency_s, tool_calls when known) and the dimensions (role, task_class, band, model, strategy, repo = "orchestrator"). `by_skill(root, group_by=("role","task_class"))` aggregates per skill × the chosen dimensions with n and every metric; unknown values are None, never 0.
2. Marginal value (P15): `marginal(root, skill, group_by=("role","task_class"), min_samples=cfg)`: for each group, compare runs of the same role/class WITH the skill used vs WITHOUT (neither used nor selected): deltas for first_pass, fix_rounds, accepted_tokens, accepted_usd, latency_s, plus the skill's own token overhead (l2 tokens per use); returns {"insufficient": True, "n_with", "n_without"} below min_samples on either side; otherwise deltas with both n. A `verdict` field: "valuable" (quality delta ≥ 0 and cost delta ≤ 0, or quality delta > +0.05 with cost delta within +10%), "neutral", "costly" (tokens up without quality change), "harmful" (quality down) — reporting only, no state changes (Stage 10 acts on it).
3. Redundancy (P16): `redundancy(root)`: for skill pairs co-used in one run: count of co-uses, overlap proxy = fraction of paths read by both (from read_economy gate rows joined by session/task when available, else None), duplicated script invocations (same script:<path> tool in both skills' declared tools), unique-findings proxy = None with a note (needs Stage 6 evidence sharing). Reported as a table with n.
4. Model and workflow interaction (P24/P25): by_skill with group_by ("model",) and ("strategy","task_class") available through the CLI: `orchestrator scorecard --skills [--by role,task_class|model|strategy,task_class] [--marginal <skill>] [--redundancy]`; `--economy` skills block gains the top-3 "costly"/"harmful" verdicts when any group has sufficient samples.
5. docs/skill-intelligence/05-scorecard.md (≤70 lines): formulas, dimensions, the verdict rules, what is a proxy, min_samples, revert path (reporting only).
Tests (unittest): tests/test_skill_scorecard.py::test_usage_rows_join_lineage_outcomes_and_dimensions, ::test_by_skill_groups_and_none_for_unknown, ::test_marginal_insufficient_below_min_samples, ::test_marginal_verdicts_valuable_costly_harmful, ::test_redundancy_pairs_and_script_overlap, ::test_cli_by_model_and_strategy. Never quote double-brace placeholder tokens literally. Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result.

SPEC v2 (2026-09-23 06:05) after spec review T-0931 (request_changes), binding on top of v1:
- orchestrator/skill_scorecard.py and tests/test_skill_scorecard.py already exist (from T-0894 and T-0913) and are EXTENDED, never replaced: add usage_rows/by_skill/marginal/redundancy next to the existing build()/format_report(); the three existing tests (test_use_rate_and_overhead_ratio_per_skill, test_skill_tokens_per_accepted_task, test_skill_recovery_rate_and_reduction) must keep passing and are listed in acceptance.
- CLI grouping: a new flag `--group-by <dims>` (comma-separated, validated against the allowed dimension names role, task_class, band, model, strategy, repo) applies to --skills mode only; the existing single-choice `--by` is untouched. `--marginal <skill>` and `--redundancy` remain as specified.
- redundancy()'s overlap proxy reads .orchestrator/runs/jev/gate.jsonl rows directly (fields session, task, tool, tool_target) and joins them to runs by task id; read_economy.summary() is not used for this.
- Acceptance adds: the three existing tests stay green; tests/test_skill_scorecard.py::test_cli_by_model_and_strategy uses --group-by.

SPEC v3 (2026-09-23 06:45) after spec review T-0934 (round 2; three points folded in, further review waived by the Planner, verdict set to approve):
- redundancy() overlap proxy, precise: for each skill build its aggregate path-set from gate rows of runs where that skill was the ONLY skill used (single-skill runs); the overlap of a pair = |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B| over those aggregate sets; co-use count is reported separately from runs where both were used; when either skill has no single-skill runs the overlap is None with note "no single-skill runs".
- usage_rows() resolves each run's owning execute-root lineage with the same task-graph membership logic as strategy._root_id (walk fix_round_for and inputs/parent links to the execute root of the task graph), so scout, spec_review and review runs inherit the outcome of the execute root they served; runs with no execute root keep outcome None.
- CLI: --group-by, --marginal and --redundancy passed without --skills are rejected with ap.error in the existing mode-conflict style; an unknown --group-by dimension is rejected the same way. Test tests/test_skill_scorecard.py::test_cli_rejects_skill_flags_without_skills_mode.
acceptance: docs/skill-intelligence/05-scorecard.md exists; `uv run orchestrator scorecard --skills --redundancy` runs; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

result.summary: Core logic, tests, docs, and CLI wiring match SPEC v2/v3 (group-by validation, mode-conflict rejection, marginal verdict rules, execute-root lineage walk, single-skill-run overlap definition). The one substantive defect is the tool-name casing mismatch in redundancy()'s gate-row filter, which makes the overlap proxy permanently return None on real data while the test suite (using synthetic lowercase tool names) masks it.

comments.issue: redundancy()'s tool filter checks row.get("tool") against lowercase ("read","search","find"), but the actual jev_gate.py hook logs the raw Claude tool_name verbatim ("Read","Grep","Glob","Edit","Write","Bash" — see jev_gate.py:140 and :344, no .lower() anywhere). In production gate.jsonl this filter never matches, so `paths` stays empty for every skill and overlap is always None with note "no single-skill runs", even when real single-skill runs with read activity exist. The unit test only passes because it fabricates gate rows with tool:"read" (lowercase), which doesn't reflect real data, so the bug is undetected by the suite. This silently defeats the P16 redundancy overlap proxy — one of this task's core deliverables — for all real usage.
